items.informal_name: Membership Criterion for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : Zero α] {s : Finset ι} {f : ι →₀ α} {t : ι → Finset α},
  f ∈ s.finsupp t ↔ f.support ⊆ s ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, f i ∈ t i
items.informal_description: A finite support function $ f $ belongs to the set $ s.\text{finsupp} \, t $ if and only if two conditions hold: (1) the support of $ f $ (i.e., the set of indices where $ f $ is non-zero) is contained in the finite set $ s $, and (2) for every index $ i \in s $, the value $ f(i) $ lies in the corresponding finite set $ t(i) $. Symbolically, $ f \in s.\text{finsupp} \, t \iff \text{support}(f) \subseteq s \land (\forall i \in s, f(i) \in t(i)) $.

items.type:

items.informal_description: For dependent finite support functions $f$ and $g$ with values in a family of locally finite ordered types $\alpha_i$, this function returns the dependent finite support function whose value at each index $i$ is the closed interval $[f(i), g(i)]$ in $\alpha_i$. The support of the resulting function is contained in the union of the supports of $f$ and $g$, ensuring finite support since both $f$ and $g$ have finite support.

Here, $ \alpha $ is a type equipped with a partial order and locally finite order structure, ensuring that each interval is finite.

items.informal_description: A dependent finite support function $ f $ belongs to the set $ s.\text{dfinsupp} \, t $ if and only if two conditions hold: (1) the support of $ f $ (the set of indices $ i $ where $ f(i) \neq 0 $) is a subset of $ s $, and (2) for every index $ i \in s $, the value $ f(i) $ lies in the corresponding finite set $ t(i) $.

items.informal_name: Support of Interval Between Dependent Finite Support Functions is Subset of Union of Supports
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : ι → Type u_2} [inst : (i : ι) → Zero (α i)] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (α i)]
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (α i)] {f g : Π₀ (i : ι), α i} [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι]
  [inst_4 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (α i)], (f.rangeIcc g).support ⊆ f.support ∪ g.support
items.informal_description: For dependent finite support functions $f$ and $g$ with values in a family of locally finite ordered types, the support of the interval function $[f(i), g(i)]$ at each index $i$ is contained in the union of the supports of $f$ and $g$. This ensures that the resulting function has finite support since both $f$ and $g$ have finite support.

items.informal_name: Closed Interval of Finite Support Functions as Product over Union of Supports
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : PartialOrder α] [inst_1 : Zero α] [inst_2 : LocallyFiniteOrder α]
  [inst_3 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_4 : DecidableEq α] (f g : ι →₀ α),
  Finset.Icc f g = (f.support ∪ g.support).finsupp ⇑(f.rangeIcc g)
items.informal_description: For finite support functions $ f $ and $ g $ with values in a locally finite ordered type $ \alpha $, the closed interval $[f, g]$ consists precisely of all finite support functions $ h $ such that $ h(i) \in [f(i), g(i)] $ for every index $ i $ in the union of the supports of $ f $ and $ g $, and $ h(i) = 0 $ otherwise. This is constructed by taking the dependent product over the union $ \operatorname{support}(f) \cup \operatorname{support}(g) $ of the intervals $[f(i), g(i)]$ at each index $ i $.
